note: Golden parse vectors for relationship-contract.v1.json. Run by the TypeScript and the Python parser. Hand-written, no customer text. Cases that depend on parse.evidenceMaxWords are named in tests, not hard-coded here.

cases.name: clean item
same item wrapped in prose and a code fence
cases.raw:
Here is my answer:
```json
{"type":"supersedes","confidence":0.9,"reason":"B replaces A"}
```

cases.name: first object wins when two are present
braces inside a string do not end the object
escaped quote and brace inside a string
object nested in an array is still the first object
unknown type is dropped
unknown type is dropped (second example)
wrong case is dropped, no case folding
surrounding space in the type is dropped
type that is not a string is dropped
missing type is dropped
a stored type outside the offer list is dropped
a stored type outside the offer list is dropped (second example)
the verdict type is dropped under the legacy offer
a type the database allows but the offer omits is dropped
a type in the offer is accepted (blocks)
confidence above one clamps to one
confidence below zero clamps to zero
confidence of exactly one passes through
confidence of exactly zero passes through
confidence inside the range passes through
missing confidence defaults
string confidence defaults, no coercion
boolean confidence defaults
null confidence defaults
NaN is not JSON, so the item is dropped
cases.note: Python json.loads accepts NaN by default; the contract is strict JSON.

cases.name: a non-breaking space does not split a word
cases.raw: {"type": "incompatible", "confidence": 0.8, "reason": "x", "evidence": {"new_quote": "w1 w2 w3 w4 w5 w6 w7 w8 w9 w10 w11 w12 w13 w14 p\u00a0q", "existing_quote": "it stays"}}

evidence.new_quote: w1 w2 w3 w4 w5 w6 w7 w8 w9 w10 w11 w12 w13 w14 p q

cases.note: Words split on ASCII space, tab, CR and LF only. 14 words plus one NBSP-joined pair is 15.
